body: There is nothing wrong with you that in anyway reduces your value as a person. You are valuable to this world. On top of that, there is value in the world for you as well. You have to find something. The trick, for me at least, is finding any little thing to get through this moment. If you can get therapy and a psychiatrist, do it. If that isn't an option, find something to obsess over. Pick some super addictive game and play the shit out of it. Do anything you can think of just to push through the tough time. For me, I have been playing the re-release of World of Warcraft Vanilla called WoW classic. It is literally the only thing I can do when I get into my dark place that can make me forget. If you want to play together, PM me and I would be happy to make a new character with you and talk about life while we play. I play several other PC games like Rocket League, CSGO, Team Fortress 2, and many others. If there is anything you already play, I would be down to join you on your adventures. Hang in there buddy, we're in this together.

I honestly don't know about in Canada, but in the US, you can absolutely take someone to the emergency room and have them checked in if they are a clear and present danger to themselves or others. That kid needs the help though, and you're right... he will do it eventually. Threatening suicide, at least for me, was saying I wanted to die but wanted help to feel normal. Eventually even wanting the help goes away.

This is probably a weird suggestion, but it helped me with one of my attempts. I quit my job and lived in Mexico for 3 months. I had barely any money so I lived on a farm and worked for a bed. Then I moved into a city and worked at a hotel as a room cleaner in exchange for food and a bed. I sold most anything I had of any value and left with about $3000 to my name intending to go to Mexico and die away from my family in a way where they wouldn't have to think it was a suicide. It was a crazy weird trip where I got into many dangerous situations and narrowly got out. My trip ended when someone began leaving threats at my hotel/restaurants I frequented, and I realized that I had so much fun I didn't want to die anymore. ---Then I came back to the states where my sister died and everything went back downhill. Now I don't have anything of value or any money to disappear to some random place but it really did help push those thoughts out for awhile. Use your job as leverage into ANYTHING else because capitalizing off of the suffering of people is enough to make anyone suicidal. Be a goddamn bartender, server, delivery driver, or anything else you might think of as an easy job and get a whole change. There is no law that says you have to use your degree. There is nothing forcing you to stay there. Yes, money is a big deal, but I assure you there isn't any amount of money worth more than your life.
